description: The bar chart illustrates the percentage composition of attention paid to different input segments – Context, Generated Response, and Other – by two models, 'Ours' and 'Standard.' The vertical axis lists the categories 'Ours' and 'Standard,' while the horizontal axis represents percentage composition, ranging from 0% to 100% with tick labels at regular intervals of 10%. Each category bar is horizontally segmented into three colored components: blue represents 'Context,' orange represents 'Generated Response,' and green represents 'Other.' For the 'Ours' model, the 'Context' segment occupies approximately 60.6%, the 'Generated Response' segment occupies approximately 31.7%, and the 'Other' segment occupies approximately 7.7%. For the 'Standard' model, the 'Context' segment occupies approximately 23.6%, the 'Generated Response' segment occupies approximately 51.1%, and the 'Other' segment occupies approximately 25.3%. The bars are arranged vertically and are not sorted in any apparent order, and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average rate at which the model attends most to each input segment: context, generated response, or other (e.g., system prompts) during generation. The vertical axis contains the categories labeled 'Ours' and 'Standard,' while the horizontal axis represents the percentage composition. Each bar is divided into three segments, with colors representing different categories: blue for 'Context,' orange for 'Generated Response,' and green for 'Other.' The 'Ours' bar is composed of approximately 60.6% Context (blue), 31.7% Generated Response (orange), and 7.7% Other (green). The 'Standard' bar consists of approximately 23.6% Context (blue), 41.1% Generated Response (orange), and 35.3% Other (green). Notably, the 'Standard' model demonstrates a significant decline in attention to Context compared to the 'Ours' model, while the attention to Other increases substantially. This suggests that the 'Standard' model prioritizes system prompts over contextual information during generation.
